headline: Chips Surge 5.9% as Energy Joins the Rally and Homebuilders Lag
body_html:
Wednesday's session belonged to chips. Semiconductors jumped 5.9%, well ahead of every other group, and the strength reached past the usual names: Sandisk gained 13.69% in memory, Applied Optoelectronics rose 15.6% in optical components, and Forgent Power Solutions added 14.34%. Of the 668 stocks we track, 462 rose and 201 fell, a clearly positive tape.

The rotation showed beneath the surface. Energy climbed 2.87%, software added 1.21%, financials 1.11%, healthcare 0.98% and industrials 0.96%. Consumer was nearly flat at 0.1% and materials slipped 0.06%, while homebuilders lost 1.37% to finish last. Energy's gain came as reports of Iran-linked disruption to shipping systems stayed in the news flow.

The standout mover was Azenta, a life-sciences tools company, which surged 20.8%, the best showing in the universe. Legence gained 15.73% and Axogen 15.21%. Declines were shallower: Tetra Tech fell 7.48%, Vital Farms 5.35% and VinFast 4.92%. The worst loser fell by less than the smallest of the top six gains. With Thursday, November 12 next, the question is whether the chip leadership broadens or leaves the rest of the market behind.

briefs.headline: Energy Rises Nearly 3% as Gulf Tensions Linger
briefs.body: Energy was the second-strongest group, up 2.87%. Reports said Iran attacked navigation systems on an island off Oman, and Saudi Arabia intercepted missiles and drones launched from Yemen. Shipping and supply risks remain part of the backdrop for crude-linked shares.

briefs.headline: OPEC+ Output Edges Back Toward Pre-War Levels
briefs.body: October production from the OPEC+ group neared the rate seen before the Iran conflict, with Saudi Arabia leading the increase. The recovery in supply is a counterweight to the regional risks that have supported energy shares.

briefs.headline: Tehran Rules Out Sending Enriched Material Abroad
briefs.body: Iran's security chief said the country will not let enriched nuclear material leave its territory. The stance adds to a diplomatic picture that remains unsettled, even as equity investors spent Wednesday focused on technology.

briefs.headline: Russia and Ukraine Report Some Progress, Washington Doubts
briefs.body: Both sides said the latest talks produced some progress. U.S. officials pointed to a lack of trust between them, a reminder that any settlement is still far off. Markets showed little visible reaction to the news.

briefs.headline: Apple's Record Run Draws a Burst of Options Activity
briefs.body: Apple's climb to new highs has brought a flurry of options trading, a sign that investors are positioning for further moves. Wednesday's session was led by chips, but large-cap technology kept drawing attention.

briefs.headline: Meta Infrastructure Chief to Depart, Ex-AWS Executive to Step In
briefs.body: Meta's head of infrastructure is leaving and will be succeeded by a former Amazon Web Services executive. The change comes as spending on computing capacity remains a central issue for the industry, and it fits the strength seen in chip-related shares.
